title: Run Here, Ship There: Which Binaries Run During the Build, Which Go to the Robot, and the Bug a Native Build Hides

questions.question: Why does a native build pass a graph with a generator built for the target?
options: The target is the host, so it runs: every mistake about which machine is invisible

questions.question: Which machine must a code generator that the build runs be built for?
options: The host, or a target the host could run
questions.explanation: A message compiler for the robot cannot run on the laptop.

questions.question: A robot program links a library that was built on the laptop. What goes wrong?
options: The library is the wrong architecture for the robot, and it fails to link or to load
questions.explanation: robot_node links libmsgs, built for the other machine.

questions.question: Is a host tool in the bundle an error the compiler reports?
options: No: it builds fine and the robot is shipped with a binary it cannot run
questions.explanation: It is a problem only a check of the graph finds.

questions.question: What does the fix cost?
options: Some tests no longer run in the build, and a library may be built twice, once for each machine
questions.explanation: A build for two machines is two builds.

questions.question: What is the real check of all this?
options: A cross build in continuous integration, which this repository does not have
questions.explanation: A passing native build tells you nothing about it.
